endpoint.text: Primary efficacy endpoint: treatment difference in change from baseline in 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) at Week 24.

citations.quote: Primary Endpoint: the primary efficacy endpoint is the treatment difference in the change in 6MWD at Week 24 compared to baseline.

result.text: Median treatment difference (Hodges-Lehmann location shift) in 6MWD at Week 24 was 40.8 meters (p<0.001) favoring sotatercept. Secondary endpoints also favored sotatercept: PVR treatment difference -234.6 dynes*sec/cm5 (p<0.001) and NT-proBNP -441.6 pg/mL (p<0.001).

citations.quote: Primary Endpoint: the primary efficacy endpoint is the treatment difference in the change in 6MWD at Week 24 compared to baseline.
The median treatment difference (Hodges-Lehmann location shift) between the sotatercept and placebo groups was 40.8 meters (p<0.001) [Table 15].
The median treatment difference between the sotatercept and placebo groups was -234.6 dynes*sec/cm5 (p<0.001) (Table 17).
The median treatment difference between the sotatercept and placebo groups was -441.6 pg/mL (p<0.001) [Table 18].

indication.text: WINREVAIR is indicated for the treatment of adults with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) to increase exercise capacity, improve WHO functional class (FC), and reduce the risk of clinical worsening events.

citations.quote: WINREVAIR™ is indicated for the treatment of adults with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, World Health Organization [WHO] Group 1) to increase exercise capacity, improve WHO functional class (FC), and reduce the risk of clinical worsening events.

target_moa.text: Sotatercept-csrk is a recombinant homodimeric activin receptor type IIA-Fc (ActRIIA-Fc) fusion protein that acts as a circulating ligand trap, binding Activin-A and other TGF-β superfamily ligands for ActRIIA to inhibit activin signaling; it is a new pharmacologic class, an activin signaling inhibitor.

citations.quote: Sotatercept-csrk consists of a recombinant homodimeric activin receptor type IIA-Fc (ActRIIA-Fc) fusion protein, which acts as a circulating ligand trap that binds activin A and other TGF-\beta superfamily ligands for ActRIIA to inhibit activin signaling.
Sotatercept acts as a ligand trap that scavenges excess Activin-A to inhibit activin signaling.
Sotatercept is a recombinant fusion protein consisting of the extracellular domain of the human activin receptor type IIA (ActRIIA) linked to the Fc portion of human IgG1.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and ≥5% more than placebo) were headache (24.5% vs 17.5%), epistaxis (22.1% vs 1.9%), rash (20.2% vs 8.1%), telangiectasia (16.6% vs 4.4%), diarrhea (15.3% vs 10.0%), dizziness (14.7% vs 6.2%), and erythema (13.5% vs 3.1%). Key risks include erythrocytosis, severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count <50,000/mm3 in 3% of patients), serious bleeding, and embryo-fetal toxicity.

citations.quote: WINREVAIR may increase hemoglobin. Severe erythrocytosis may increase the risk of thromboembolic events or hyperviscosity syndrome.
severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count <50,000/\text{mm}^3 [<50 \times 10^9/\text{L}]) occurred in 3% of patients taking WINREVAIR.
In clinical studies, serious bleeding (e.g., gastrointestinal, intracranial hemorrhage) was reported in 4% of patients taking WINREVAIR and 1% of patients taking placebo.
Based on findings in animal reproduction studies, WINREVAIR may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman.

requirement.text: 4590-1 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Winerevair (sotatercept-csrk) during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol.
